definition_zh: 淋浴；阵雨；送礼聚会；大量给予
definition_en: a wash under falling water, a short fall of rain, a party for giving gifts, or to give many things
core_image: 花洒喷出细密水线，热气在浴室里升起
scene: 他每天早上冲个淋浴。 He takes a shower every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 shower 是「淋浴」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天早上冲个淋浴。

derivatives.zh: 多阵雨的
花洒
沐浴露
浴帽

senses.title: A wash
senses.definition: a wash under a spray of falling water
senses.definitionCN: 在落下的水流下洗澡
senses.example: He takes a shower every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上冲个淋浴。
senses.why: This is the everyday bathroom sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常浴室场景中的义项。

senses.title: A rain
senses.definition: a short fall of rain
senses.definitionCN: 短时间的一阵降雨
senses.example: A shower passed over the town.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵雨掠过了小镇。
senses.why: Falling water connects rain and washing.
senses.whyCN: 落下的水流把雨和淋浴联系起来。

senses.title: A gift party
senses.definition: a party where gifts are given, especially for a baby or a bride
senses.definitionCN: 赠送礼物的聚会，尤指为婴儿或新娘举办
senses.example: They held a baby shower for her.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。
senses.why: Gifts fall on the guest like rain.
senses.whyCN: 礼物像雨一样落在客人身上。

senses.title: To give much
senses.definition: to give someone many things or much attention
senses.definitionCN: 给某人许多东西或大量关注
senses.example: Fans showered her with flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝们纷纷给她送花。
senses.why: The rain image turns into an abundance of gifts.
senses.whyCN: 雨的意象转化为礼物的丰盛。

intro.en: Shower first meant a brief fall of rain.
intro.cn: shower 最初意为一阵短暂的降雨。

items.en: Scur meant a brief storm or shower.
items.cn: scur 意为短暂的暴风雨或阵雨。

items.en: Shour named a fall of rain.
items.cn: shour 指一阵降雨。

items.en: The washing sense appeared with indoor plumbing.
items.cn: 随着室内管道出现，淋浴义项产生了。

items.en: A party for giving gifts took the name.
items.cn: 赠送礼物的聚会沿用了这个词。

items.en: The verb came to mean to give in large amounts.
items.cn: 动词义发展为大量给予。

note.en: Shower is compared with similar-looking words and with words for washing and rain.
note.cn: 把 shower 与形近词以及表示洗浴和降雨的词作比较。

definition_zh: 在室内；进入室内
definition_en: into or inside a building; within a house
core_image: 从门口走进屋檐的那一步
scene: 外面下起大雨，猫第一个溜进了屋里。 The children stayed indoors all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 indoors 是「在室内」（第 1 个义项：处于屋内）；句意：孩子们整个下午都待在室内。

derivatives.zh: 反义副词，义为「在户外」

senses.title: Within a building
senses.definition: inside a house or building
senses.definitionCN: 在房屋或建筑物里面
senses.example: Stay indoors until the storm passes.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过去之前请待在室内。
senses.why: The roof above is the whole map.
senses.whyCN: 头顶的屋顶就是全部地图。

senses.title: Into a building
senses.definition: moving from outside to inside
senses.definitionCN: 从外面走进里面
senses.example: Everyone hurried indoors when it rained.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨时大家匆匆进了屋。
senses.why: One step across the doorway.
senses.whyCN: 跨过门槛的一步。

senses.title: Opposite of outdoors
senses.definition: the word paired against outdoor life
senses.definitionCN: 与户外生活相对的词
senses.example: He prefers indoors to the hot sun.
senses.exampleCN: 比起烈日他更愿意待在室内。
senses.why: Inside and outside stand face to face.
senses.whyCN: 屋内与屋外面对面。

intro.en: Indoors is a compound of in + doors, formed in English. The odd plural is a fossil: the word came from the phrase within doors.
intro.cn: indoors 是英语内造的复合词，由 in + doors 构成。复数形式是化石：它来自短语 within doors「在门之内」。

items.en: Old English duru meant door; its plural became doors.
items.cn: 古英语 duru 意为门，复数为 doors。

items.en: The phrase within doors meant inside the house's doors.
items.cn: 短语 within doors 指屋门之内。

items.en: A shorter form at doors also meant inside.
items.cn: 更简的形式 at doors 同样指在屋内。

items.en: English fused in with doors into the adverb indoors.
items.cn: 现代英语把 in 与 doors 融合成副词 indoors。

items.en: Later the adjective indoor dropped the s by analogy with outdoor.
items.cn: 后来类比 outdoor，形容词 indoor 去掉了 s。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the door family. The meaning group compares words of being inside.
note.cn: 形近组收录 door 词族；词义组比较表示「在内」的词。

abstract.en: The roof is the ceiling of your world indoors.

examples.en: The pool is outdoors but the gym is indoors.

root: 英语短语 within doors / at doors「门之内」→ 压缩融合为复合副词 indoors「在室内」；与 outdoor 类比得形容词 indoor。

sensesIntro.en: Indoors is the doorway step: being under a roof, crossing in from the rain, and the mirror word outdoors.
sensesIntro.cn: indoors 是门槛上那一步：在屋顶之下、从雨里跨进屋，以及镜子对面的 outdoors。

core.cn: 门口温暖的一侧：在屋顶下而非天底下。

definition_zh: 哭；流泪；叫喊；大声呼喊
definition_en: to shed tears, often with sound; to shout or call out loudly
core_image: 眼泪冲出眼眶、声音从喉咙冲出
scene: 运动会接力赛输了，队友们都红了眼眶，可谁也没放弃下一场。 She wanted to cry when she missed the last basket.
sceneCN: 这里 cry 是「哭」（第 1 个义项：流出眼泪并常带哭声）；句意是她投丢最后一球时想哭。

collocations.zh: 为无法挽回的事哭泣（谚语）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「哭着的；紧急的」
由 cry 加 baby 构成，义为「爱哭的人」
由 out 加 cry 构成，义为「强烈抗议」

senses.title: To shed tears from feeling
senses.definition: to let tears fall because you are sad, hurt or even overjoyed
senses.definitionCN: 因伤心、受伤甚至过度高兴而让眼泪落下
senses.example: The little boy cried when his balloon flew away.
senses.exampleCN: 气球飞走时，小男孩哭了。
senses.why: The core image is tears bursting out when feelings overflow, so strong emotion makes people cry.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是情感满溢时眼泪夺眶而出，所以强烈的情绪让人 cry。

senses.title: To shout loudly
senses.definition: to call out in a loud voice, often to warn or attract attention
senses.definitionCN: 大声呼喊，常为了提醒或引人注意
senses.example: Watch out! she cried as the ball flew over.
senses.exampleCN: 球飞过来时她大喊：小心！
senses.why: The same burst that pushes tears out can push sound out, so the voice cry joins the tear cry.
senses.whyCN: 把眼泪冲出来的那股爆发力也能把声音冲出来，所以声音的呼喊与眼泪的哭共用一词。

senses.title: A loud call or slogan
senses.definition: a loud sound, shout or slogan heard from a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体发出的响亮喊声或口号
senses.example: We heard the cry of vendors selling hot potatoes outside the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见体育场外卖烤红薯小贩的叫卖声。
senses.why: When many voices rise together, each burst becomes a cry that can be heard and even written down.
senses.whyCN: 当许多声音一齐响起时，每次爆发都成为可听见甚至可记录的 cry。

intro.en: Cry came through French from a Latin word about outcry and prayer.
intro.cn: cry 经法语来自拉丁语中与呼喊、祈祷相关的词。

items.en: The Latin quiritare meant to shriek, said to come from calling on the Quirites, Roman citizens, for help.
items.cn: 拉丁语 quiritare 意为尖叫，一般认为源自向罗马公民（Quirites）呼救。

items.en: Old French carried it as crier, meaning to shout or proclaim.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 crier，意为喊叫、宣告。

items.en: English borrowed crien in the thirteenth century for loud calls.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 crien，指大声呼喊。

items.en: The tearful sense grew beside the shouting sense.
items.cn: 流泪义在喊叫义旁边生长出来。

items.en: Today cry covers tears, shouts, slogans and street calls.
items.cn: 如今 cry 覆盖眼泪、喊叫、口号与街头叫卖。

note.en: These words share the cry family or name tears and shouts.
note.cn: 这些词属于 cry 词族，或指眼泪与喊叫。

abstract.en: Feel the hot lump rise in your throat before tears fall.
abstract.cn: 感受眼泪落下前喉咙里的热块。

abstract.en: Hear a watchman's voice ring across the quiet street.
abstract.cn: 听守夜人的声音在安静的街道回荡。

abstract.en: See one word shouted by a hundred fans as one slogan.
abstract.cn: 看百名球迷把一个词喊成口号。

examples.en: The film's ending was so touching that many of us cried.
examples.cn: 电影结尾太感人，我们许多人都哭了。

examples.en: He heard a cry for help from the swimming pool.
examples.cn: 他听到游泳池传来呼救声。

examples.en: Don't cry over the broken vase; it was an accident.
examples.cn: 别为打碎的花瓶哭了，那只是个意外。

branches.cn: 伤感电影与失利比赛的眼泪

definition_zh: 停留；留下；仍然是；剩下
definition_en: to stay in the same place or condition, or to be left after other things have gone
core_image: 人都走光了，桌上还剩着一只没被收走的杯子
scene: 散场之后，几个学生没有立刻离开，他们留在座位上继续讨论那道题。 After the lecture, a few students remained in their seats to argue about the problem.
sceneCN: 这里 remain 是「停留、留下」（第 1 个义项：没有离开原处）；句意：讲座结束后，几个学生留在座位上继续争论那道题。

derivatives.zh: remain 加 -s 构成的名词，义为「残余；遗迹；遗体」
remain 加 -der 构成，义为「剩余部分」
remain 加 -ing 构成，义为「剩余的」

senses.title: To stay in a place
senses.definition: to stay in the same place instead of leaving with the others
senses.definitionCN: 留在原处，而不随其他人离开
senses.example: Only two guests remained after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜过后，只有两位客人还留在那里。
senses.why: The Latin verb manere means to stay, and re- adds the idea of staying behind, which gives the plain physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 manere 意为「停留」，前缀 re- 带来「留在后面」的意味，于是形成最直白的空间义。

senses.title: To continue to be in a state
senses.definition: to continue to be in a particular condition without changing
senses.definitionCN: 继续保持某种状态而不改变
senses.example: The streets remained empty all night.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜街道都空无一人。
senses.why: Staying in a place widens into staying in a condition, such as silence or safety.
senses.whyCN: 「留在某处」扩展为「留在某种状态里」，例如沉默或安全。

senses.title: To be left over
senses.definition: to still exist after other parts have been used, taken, or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 在其他部分被使用、拿走或毁掉之后仍然存在
senses.example: Little remained of the old town after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 大火之后，老城几乎没有剩下什么。
senses.why: What stays behind when everyone and everything else has gone is precisely what remains.
senses.whyCN: 当其他人和物都离开或消失后仍留在原地的，正是「剩下的」。

intro.en: Remain comes from Old French remaindre, from Latin remanere, built on re- and manere, to stay.
intro.cn: remain 来自古法语 remaindre，源自拉丁语 remanere，由 re- 与 manere「停留」构成。

items.en: Remanere means to stay behind or to be left, from re- and manere.
items.cn: remanere 意为留在后面或剩下，由 re- 与 manere 构成。

items.en: Manere is also the source of mansion and permanent, both about staying.
items.cn: manere 也是 mansion 与 permanent 的来源，两者都与「停留」有关。

items.en: Remaindre means to stay, to last, and to be left over.
items.cn: 古法语 remaindre 表示停留、持续以及剩下。

items.en: English remain covers staying in a place and continuing in a state.
items.cn: 英语 remain 同时覆盖留在某地与保持某种状态。

items.en: The plural noun remains develops separately for leftovers, ruins, and the bodies of the dead.
items.cn: 复数名词 remains 另行发展出剩饭、遗迹与遗体等含义。

note.en: Remain is the verb of staying, and its family includes the noun remains and the adjective remaining.
note.cn: remain 是表示「停留」的动词，词族包括名词 remains 与形容词 remaining。

entries.definitionCN: 残余；遗迹；遗体，由 remain 加 -s 构成

entries.definition: still present when the rest has gone

entries.definition: the part that is left over

entries.definition: to continue to be in a place

entries.definition: to stay somewhere longer than necessary
entries.definitionCN: 逗留；徘徊，带有不愿离开的意味

entries.definition: to continue to exist or happen

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb manere, to stay, is the spine of this word and of mansion and permanent.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 manere「停留」是这个词的骨架，也支撑着 mansion 与 permanent。

normal.en: Re- plus manere gives staying behind while everyone else moves on.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 manere，就是别人都走了，它还留在后面。

normal.en: Mansion and permanent share the same root, one a place that stays, one a state that lasts.
normal.cn: mansion 与 permanent 共享同一词根，一个是留下来的房子，一个是持续的状态。

normal.en: Add -s and the word becomes a noun for leftovers and ruins.
normal.cn: 加 -s 就变成名词，指剩饭与遗迹。

normal.en: The pattern remain silent teaches the linking use: remain plus adjective.
normal.cn: remain silent 这个搭配说明了它的连系用法：remain 加形容词。

normal.en: It remains to be seen is a fixed sentence opener in news writing.
normal.cn: it remains to be seen 是新闻写作中固定的句子开头。

abstract.en: Picture a single cup on a table after the whole party has left.
abstract.cn: 想象聚会散尽后，桌上只留下一个杯子。

abstract.en: See a lighthouse still standing after the village has been abandoned.
abstract.cn: 想象村庄废弃之后，灯塔仍然立着。

abstract.en: Think of a light left on in a window all night.
abstract.cn: 想一扇窗里彻夜亮着的灯。

examples.en: Please remain seated until the plane has stopped.
examples.cn: 飞机停稳之前请留在座位上。

examples.en: The reason for the delay remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 延误的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: Very little remained of the original building.
examples.cn: 原来的建筑几乎没有剩下什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞梅」——梅花谢了，枝上还剩一朵；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 remaindre，源自拉丁语 remanere（re-「留在后面」+ manere「停留」）。

sensesIntro.en: Staying in a place becomes staying in a state and then being what is left when everything else is gone.
sensesIntro.cn: 留在某处，进而变成留在某种状态，再变成其他一切消失后尚存的部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cup left on the table after everyone has gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：人都走光后，桌上还剩一只杯子。

branches.en: The cup stays where it was, which is the plain sense of remaining in place.
branches.cn: 杯子留在原处，这就是最直白的「停留」义。

branches.en: Staying in a place stretches into staying in a condition.
branches.cn: 留在某处被拉长成留在某种状态里。

branches.en: When everything else is taken away, what stays is what is left over.
branches.cn: 其他一切被拿走之后，留下来的就是剩余之物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the same stillness at the centre.
branches.cn: 两个义项的中心都是同一种静止不动。

branches.en: Physical staying and ongoing state share one root, manere.
branches.cn: 空间上的停留与状态的延续共享同一个词根 manere。

intro.en: Remain is a French-shaped verb whose Latin prefix and root still show in related words.
intro.cn: remain 是法语形态的动词，其拉丁前缀与词根在相关词中仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back or behind, and manere means to stay, so the verb means to stay behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「回、在后」，manere 表示「停留」，合起来即「留在后面」。

items.example: Re- gives the sense of staying behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 带来「留在后面」的含义。

items.example: The man- root returns in mansion and permanent.
items.exampleCN: man- 词根也出现在 mansion 与 permanent 中。

items.example: Manere is the verb at the heart of remain.
items.exampleCN: manere 是 remain 的核心动词。

items.meaning: more than one, or a mass noun
items.example: Remains turns the verb into a plural noun.
items.exampleCN: remains 把动词变成复数名词。

items.example: Remaining describes what is still there.
items.exampleCN: remaining 描述依然存在的部分。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作结果的名词词尾
items.example: Remainder names the part left over.
Mansion keeps the sense of a place where one stays.
items.exampleCN: mansion 保留了「停留之所」的含义。

items.example: Permanent adds per- to the same manere root.
items.exampleCN: permanent 在同一个 manere 词根前加了 per-。

definition_zh: 杯子；一杯之量；奖杯
definition_en: a small round container for drinking; the amount it holds; a prize
core_image: 双手捧起的一个小圆容器
scene: 跑完八百米，同学递给我水壶，我一口气喝了半瓶。 She poured some warm water into a cup for the tired runner.
sceneCN: 这里 cup 是「杯子」（第 1 个义项：喝水用的小圆容器）；句意是她给疲惫的跑者往杯子里倒了些温水。

derivatives.zh: 由 cup 加 -ful 构成，义为「一满杯」
由 cup 加 board 构成，义为「碗柜；橱柜」
由 tea 加 cup 构成，义为「茶杯」

senses.title: A small round drinking container
senses.definition: a small round container with a handle, used for hot drinks
senses.definitionCN: 带把手的小圆容器，常用来喝热饮
senses.example: Grandpa holds his cup with both hands because the tea is hot.
senses.exampleCN: 茶太烫，爷爷双手捧着杯子。
senses.why: Hands naturally curve to hold liquid, so the round open shape got a name of its own.
senses.whyCN: 双手捧水时会自然弯成弧形，这种圆口盛液的形状便有了自己的名字。

senses.title: The amount a cup holds
senses.definition: the quantity that a cup can contain, often in recipes
senses.definitionCN: 一个杯子能装下的量，常用于菜谱
senses.example: Add a cup of milk to the cake mixture.
senses.exampleCN: 往蛋糕糊里加一杯牛奶。
senses.why: The container became a unit of measure because cooks poured by cupfuls.
senses.whyCN: 厨师们按杯倒料，容器便变成了计量单位。

senses.title: A prize in a competition
senses.definition: a silver or gold cup given as a prize in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛获胜者获得的金银奖杯
senses.example: Our school team won the cup at the football final.
senses.exampleCN: 我们校队在足球决赛中赢得了奖杯。
senses.why: A fine cup was once a precious gift for winners, so the award took the container's name.
senses.whyCN: 精致的杯子曾是献给优胜者的贵重礼物，于是奖项借用了容器的名字。

intro.en: Cup goes back to a Latin word for a small tub or cask.
intro.cn: cup 可以追溯到拉丁语中指小桶、小盆的词。

items.en: The word cuppa meant a small cask or basin for drinking.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cuppa 指饮用的小桶或小盆。

items.en: English borrowed it early as cuppe, meaning a drinking vessel.
items.cn: 英语很早借入 cuppe，指饮水器皿。

items.en: By medieval times cup also meant the measure and the prize chalice.
items.cn: 中世纪时 cup 也表示容量单位和奖赏用的杯盏。

items.en: Compound words like cupboard appeared, naming furniture that once stored cups.
items.cn: cupboard 之类的复合词出现，命名曾用来存放杯子的家具。

items.en: Today cup names tableware, a recipe measure and sports trophies.
items.cn: 如今 cup 既指餐具，也指菜谱计量单位和体育奖杯。

note.en: These words name drinking containers or similar small vessels.
note.cn: 这些词指饮水容器或类似的小型器皿。

entries.definition: the amount that fills a cup
a cabinet for storing dishes and food
a small cup for tea
a young lion or bear; sounds like cup but means a baby animal
entries.definitionCN: 幼兽（发音近似 cup，词义无关）

entries.definition: a drinking container made of glass
a tall cup without a saucer
a deep round dish for food
a container with a narrow neck for liquids

normalIntro.en: Use everyday tableware words to fix the spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 用身边的餐具词把拼写记牢。

normal.en: cup + ful = cupful, one full cup.
normal.cn: cup + ful ＝ cupful（一满杯）。

normal.en: cup + board = cupboard, the old cup shelf; now said KUB-erd.
normal.cn: cup + board ＝ cupboard（碗柜），口语读成 KUB-erd。

normal.en: tea + cup = teacup, a cup only for tea.
normal.cn: tea + cup ＝ teacup（茶杯）。

normal.en: One p, one u: cup, not copp or cuup.
normal.cn: 一个 p 一个 u：cup，别写成 copp 或 cuup。

normal.en: A World Cup is the biggest cup prize in football.
normal.cn: 世界杯（World Cup）是足球界最大的杯状奖杯。

abstract.en: Picture both hands curling around warm tea on a cold morning.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷清晨双手捧起热茶的弧度。

abstract.en: See the recipe line: one cup of sugar, level and exact.
abstract.cn: 看菜谱那一行：一平杯糖，不多不少。

abstract.en: Feel team members lifting a silver cup over their heads.
abstract.cn: 想象队员们把银奖杯高高举过头顶。

examples.en: Mum made me a hot cup of milk before bed.
examples.cn: 睡前妈妈给我冲了一杯热牛奶。

examples.en: Please wash the cups after the tea party.
examples.cn: 茶会结束后请把杯子洗一洗。

examples.en: They cheered when the captain raised the cup.
examples.cn: 队长举起奖杯时，大家欢呼起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡普」——杯口「卡」得正合适，正好一口「普」通的水

root: 来自拉丁语 cuppa（小桶、小盆），经古英语 cuppe 进入英语，本指饮水器皿，后引申为容量单位和奖杯。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a drinking vessel to a measure and then a prize.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从饮水器皿扩展到计量单位，再到奖品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding a small round vessel
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧着一个圆形小容器

branches.en: Cups, mugs and glasses for drinks
branches.cn: 喝水用的杯子、马克杯

branches.en: Cupfuls in cooking
branches.cn: 做饭时按杯计量

branches.en: Cups as trophies in sport
branches.cn: 体育比赛中的奖杯

branches.en: The container defines the amount

branches.en: Full measure earns the prize
branches.cn: 满满的成绩换来奖杯

intro.cn: cup 是个短词，喜欢和其他词组合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin parent cuppa meant a small tub.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖先 cuppa 意为小桶。

definition_zh: 高度地；非常；赞许地
definition_en: to a great degree, or with strong praise
core_image: 把刻度推到顶端的那个推杆
scene: 老师把新来的同学推荐给校辩论队，称赞他逻辑清晰、台风稳健。 The coach spoke highly of the new debater before the match began.
sceneCN: 这里 highly 是「高度地；赞许地」（第 1 个义项：程度极高）；教练在赛前高度称赞新队员。

derivatives.zh: highly 的基础形容词，义为「高的」
同根名词，义为「高度」
复合动词，义为「突出；强调」

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: to a very great degree or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在程度或数量上非常大
senses.example: It is highly likely that the train will be late.
senses.exampleCN: 火车很有可能晚点。
senses.why: The adverb pushes the adjective's scale toward the top.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词的刻度推向顶端。

senses.title: With strong praise
senses.definition: with admiration or strong approval
senses.definitionCN: 带着钦佩或强烈认可
senses.example: Doctors think highly of this new medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们对这种新药评价很高。
senses.why: Praise lifts a person high on the social scale.
senses.whyCN: 赞扬把人抬到社会刻度的高处。

intro.en: Highly simply adds the adverb suffix -ly to high.
intro.cn: highly 只是在 high 后加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: The base hēah already had adverbial uses.
items.cn: 基础词 hēah 早已兼作副词使用。

items.en: Middle English formed heghely with the -ly ending.
items.cn: 中古英语用 -ly 词尾构成 heghely。

items.en: The suffix -ly comes from Old English -lice, a native ending.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，是本族词尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps highly mainly for abstract degrees and praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中 highly 主要用于抽象程度与赞扬。

items.en: Phrases like speak highly of became fixed collocations.
items.cn: speak highly of 等短语固化为固定搭配。

note.en: Compare highly with its base and rivals.
note.cn: 把 highly 与基础词及竞争词对照。

entries.definitionCN: 基础形容词「高的」，可兼作实体副词

entries.definition: noun form of high
main road

entries.definition: to a great degree, plain register
to the highest degree
spoken of with approval

normalIntro.en: Anchor highly in its two fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 用两个固定短语锚定 highly。

normal.en: speak highly of = praise strongly.
normal.cn: speak highly of 就是「高度赞扬」。

normal.en: think highly of = value someone greatly.
normal.cn: think highly of 就是「非常器重」。

normal.en: highly likely appears in weather and news.
normal.cn: highly likely 常出现在天气预报和新闻里。

normal.en: highly is for abstract degrees; high is for real height.
normal.cn: highly 用于抽象程度；high 用于实际高度。

normal.en: He flew high, and critics rated him highly.
normal.cn: 他飞得高（high），评价也高（highly）——一句话分开两词。

abstract.en: Picture a slider pushed all the way up.
abstract.cn: 想象一根滑杆被推到最顶端——highly 的程度感。

abstract.en: Feel highly as a judge raising a score card.
abstract.cn: 把 highly 感受成裁判举起高分牌。

abstract.en: Hear applause rising after speak highly of.
abstract.cn: 听见 speak highly of 之后升起的掌声。

examples.en: The film was highly praised by local critics.
examples.cn: 这部电影受到本地影评人的高度赞扬。

examples.en: It is highly unlikely that snow will fall today.
examples.cn: 今天下雪的可能性极低。

examples.en: She is a highly experienced nurse in this hospital.
examples.cn: 她是这家医院经验非常丰富的护士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨来」——「嗨，来了个特别厉害的」，程度拉满正是 highly。

sensesIntro.en: Highly raises degrees and raises praise.

branches.cn: 程度推到很高（义项 01）

branches.cn: 强烈表达的赞许（义项 02）

branches.en: the high end of any scale
branches.cn: 任何刻度的高端（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: probability and quantity boosters
branches.cn: 可能性与数量的放大词（义项 01）

branches.en: words of professional respect
branches.cn: 表达业内敬重的措辞（义项 02）

intro.en: The -ly suffix turns adjectives into adverbs of manner or degree.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变为方式或程度副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin uses -ter for adverbs; English -ly is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 -ter 构成副词；英语 -ly 是本族词尾。

over a large area or extent

items.example: Guests spoke highly of the hotel.
items.exampleCN: 客人们对这家酒店评价很高。

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的
definition_en: giving pleasure to the senses or the mind; also friendly in manner, or agreeable as an experience
core_image: 推开门的一瞬间，暖风、光线和淡淡香气一起涌上来，人不由自主放松了肩膀
scene: 午后的花园里风很轻，桌上刚切开的柠檬散出清香。 The garden felt pleasant in the soft afternoon light.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人愉快的、宜人的」（第 1 个义项）；句意为在柔和的午后光线里，这座花园让人感到惬意。图中可辨识物件：柠檬、白桌布、树影。

pos.zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的

derivatives.zh: pleasant 的同源动词，义为「使高兴；请」
由 please 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「愉快；乐事」
由 pleasant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pleasant 构成，义为「令人不快的」

senses.title: Giving pleasure to the senses
senses.definition: giving a feeling of enjoyment to the senses, as a place, smell, sound or taste does
senses.definitionCN: 让感官产生愉悦，如地方、气味、声音或味道带来的舒服感
senses.example: The room was small but pleasant, with wide windows and warm light.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大却很宜人，窗户宽大，光线温暖。
senses.why: The word began as the present participle of the verb to please, so anything pleasant is literally something that is pleasing you while you experience it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是动词 please 的现在分词，所以凡是 pleasant 的东西，字面上就是正在让你愉悦的东西。

senses.title: Friendly and agreeable in manner
senses.definition: kind, polite and easy to be with, said of a person or a person's manner
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或其举止亲切、有礼、好相处
senses.example: Our host gave us a pleasant smile and showed us to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 主人朝我们和善地一笑，把我们引到桌边。
senses.why: If a thing can please, a person can please too; the adjective then moves from the effect on the senses to the social warmth of someone's behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 既然事物能使人愉悦，人也能使人愉悦；于是这个形容词从感官效果转到某人举止带来的社交暖意。

senses.title: Agreeable to the mind
senses.definition: satisfying or welcome as a piece of news, a task or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指消息、任务或安排令人满意、受欢迎
senses.example: It was a pleasant change to finish work before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天没黑就干完活，这种改变让人舒心。
senses.why: Beyond the senses lies the mind: what fits our plans and leaves us easy is also called pleasant, which shows how far the pleasing image can reach.
senses.whyCN: 感官之外还有心智：合乎计划、让人安心的事也被称作 pleasant，可见「使人愉悦」这幅画面能延伸多远。

intro.en: Pleasant and please come from one Latin verb, but they entered English as different parts of speech: please as a verb, pleasant as its participle turned adjective.
intro.cn: pleasant 与 please 同出一个拉丁动词，但进入英语时词性不同：please 是动词，pleasant 是由它的分词转成的形容词。

items.en: The verb placere meant to please, to be agreeable, and it was used of things that satisfy a person.
items.cn: 动词 placere 意为使人高兴、令人满意，用来指让人称心的事物。

items.en: Its present participle placens, stem placent-, meant pleasing, the one giving pleasure.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）意为「令人愉悦的」，即正在带来愉悦的那一方。

items.en: Old French turned the participle into plaisant, an adjective meaning pleasing or charming.
items.cn: 古法语把这个分词变成形容词 plaisant，意为令人愉悦的、讨人喜欢的。

items.en: English borrowed plaisant as pleasant, keeping the adjective role, while the verb came in separately as please.
items.cn: 英语借入 plaisant 写作 pleasant，保留形容词身份；动词则另以 please 的形式进入。

items.en: Modern English uses pleasant for places, manners and news, and please for the act of giving pleasure or making a request.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pleasant 形容地方、举止与消息，用 please 表示使人高兴的动作或礼貌请求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the please family and one word with a different origin; the near-meaning group gathers words for what delights or suits us.
note.cn: 形近组收 please 词族，以及一个来源不同的词；近义组收表示使人愉悦或合宜的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give pleasure or to ask politely; pleasant is its old participle.
entries.definitionCN: 表示使人高兴或礼貌请求的动词；pleasant 是它古老的分词形式。

entries.definition: A feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.
Giving pleasure, often of an experience.
entries.definitionCN: 带来愉悦的，常形容体验。

entries.definition: An urgent request or a statement in court; looks close but comes from Old French plait, a lawsuit.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急请求或法庭陈述；拼写相近，但出自古法语 plait（诉讼），词源不同。

entries.definition: Pleasant and easy to accept or be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快、容易相处或接受的。

entries.definition: Causing great pleasure.
Giving enjoyment, said of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 令人享受的，多形容活动。

entries.definition: Pleasant or satisfactory in a general, everyday way.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中泛指令人愉快或满意的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of pleasing produced both a verb and an adjective in English; keeping their parts of speech apart is the whole trick.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「使人高兴」的拉丁动词在英语里同时产出了动词和形容词；分清两者的词性就是全部关键。

normal.en: Pleasant is the old participle of please: pleasing, therefore pleasant.
normal.cn: pleasant 是 please 古老的分词形式：正在使人愉悦的，因此是「令人愉快的」。

normal.en: Please is what you do; pleasant is what something is. The verb acts, the adjective describes.
normal.cn: please 是你做的动作；pleasant 是某物的性质。动词做事，形容词描述。

normal.en: Pleasure is the noun of the same family, formed with -ure, naming the feeling itself.
normal.cn: pleasure 是同族的动词名词，用 -ure 构成，指那种感觉本身。

normal.en: Pleasantly adds -ly to the adjective, turning it into the way something is done or felt.
normal.cn: pleasantly 在形容词后加 -ly，把它变成做某事或感受某事的方式。

normal.en: Plea looks similar but belongs to law and requests, not to pleasing.
normal.cn: plea 看着相近，却属于法律与请求的语义，与「愉悦」无关。

abstract.en: The same root gives a verb, an adjective and a noun, which shows how English lets one act spread across three roles.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出动词、形容词和名词，说明英语让一个动作分散到三种角色上。

abstract.en: A word that starts as an action becomes a quality: what pleases for long enough is simply pleasant.
abstract.cn: 一个从动作开始的词变成了性质：使人愉悦得够久，就干脆成了「令人愉快的」。

abstract.en: We call both air and manners pleasant, as if comfort in the body and comfort in company were the same feeling.
abstract.cn: 我们既说空气 pleasant，也说举止 pleasant，仿佛身体的舒适与相处时的舒适是同一种感受。

examples.en: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The staff were pleasant and quick to help.
examples.cn: 员工们态度和善，帮忙很及时。

examples.en: It was a pleasant surprise to see her at the door.
examples.cn: 在门口见到她，是个令人惊喜的意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普莱增特」——一进门就请（please）你坐下，气氛一下子变得舒服。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使人高兴）→ 现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）→ 古法语 plaisant → 英语 pleasant；同族的动词是 please。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of pleasing; the senses spread from the effect on the senses to the warmth of a person and to what suits the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使人愉悦」这个动作；义项从对感官的作用，扩展到人的和善，再到合乎心意之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opens and warmth, light and a faint scent arrive together, so the shoulders loosen without being told.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，暖意、光线与淡淡香气一同涌来，肩膀不必吩咐就松了下来。

branches.en: a wide window and warm light in a small room
branches.cn: 小房间里一扇宽窗与温暖的光

branches.en: a host smiling and pointing to a chair
branches.cn: 主人微笑并示意一把椅子

branches.en: work finished before the sky goes dark
branches.cn: 天还没黑就干完了活

branches.en: comfort that comes from people and from timing
branches.cn: 来自人、也来自时机的舒适

branches.en: the same word for air, music and taste
branches.cn: 同一个词用于空气、音乐与味道

intro.en: A Latin verb of pleasing supplies the root, its participle ending supplies the shape, and French passes the adjective to English.
intro.cn: 一个表示「使人高兴」的拉丁动词提供词根，它的分词词尾提供外形，法语再把形容词传给英语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 刷子；画笔；刷、梳；轻擦而过；灌木丛
definition_en: a tool with stiff hairs used for cleaning, painting or tidying, to use such a tool, to touch something lightly while passing, or a mass of low bushes
core_image: 一排密密的硬毛扎在木柄上
scene: 画室里，她把笔尖在颜料盘上轻轻一转，然后落在纸上。 She dipped the brush in paint and began to draw.
sceneCN: 这里 brush 是「刷子；画笔」（第 1 个义项：带硬毛或软毛的工具）；句意为她把画笔蘸上颜料，开始作画。

derivatives.zh: 由 brush 加 -y 构成，义为「毛多的；灌木丛生的」
由 brush 加 -ing 构成，义为「刷；梳」
由 brush 与 work 组合而成，义为「笔触；运笔手法」

senses.title: The tool with stiff hairs
senses.definition: a tool made of stiff hairs or bristles fixed to a handle, used for cleaning, painting or tidying
senses.definitionCN: 把硬毛或鬃毛固定在柄上做成的工具，用来清洁、绘画或整理
senses.example: She dipped the brush in paint and began to draw.
senses.exampleCN: 她把画笔蘸上颜料，开始作画。
senses.why: Old French brosse named a bundle of twigs used for scrubbing, and that bundle of hairs is still the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 brosse 指用来擦洗的一束细枝，那束毛状物至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: To clean or tidy with a brush
senses.definition: to clean, smooth or tidy something with a brush
senses.definitionCN: 用刷子清洁、抹平或整理某物
senses.example: He brushes his teeth twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天刷两次牙。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, naming the repeated stroke that the tool makes.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，用来指这件工具所做的一来一回的动作。

senses.title: To touch lightly in passing
senses.definition: to touch someone or something lightly while moving past
senses.definitionCN: 经过时轻轻碰到某人或某物
senses.example: Her sleeve brushed against my arm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的袖子擦过我的手臂。
senses.why: A brush stroke is light, so the verb came to mean any light touch that barely makes contact.
senses.whyCN: 刷一下本来就很轻，于是这个动词也指几乎没怎么碰到的轻轻一触。

senses.title: Low bushes and twigs
senses.definition: a mass of small bushes and broken twigs, used without a plural
senses.definitionCN: 一片低矮的灌木与断枝，不用复数形式
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared into the brush.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子钻进灌木丛不见了。
senses.why: The same word names the cut twigs that once made brushes, and later the low growth they came from.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指从前扎刷子的断枝，也指后来生长这些枝条的矮丛。

intro.en: Brush came from French and goes back to a Latin name for a twiggy shrub used in cleaning.
intro.cn: brush 来自法语，可上溯到拉丁语中一种枝条细密、可用来擦洗的灌木之名。

items.en: Bruscus named butcher's broom, a stiff shrub whose twigs were tied for scrubbing.
items.cn: bruscus 指假叶树，一种枝条硬挺、可扎起来擦洗的灌木。

items.en: French brosse meant a brush, both the bundle of twigs and the tool.
items.cn: 法语 brosse 意为刷子，既指一束细枝，也指工具本身。

items.en: English borrowed brush in the fourteenth century for the cleaning tool.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 brush，指清洁用的工具。

items.en: The tool turned into a verb, and light passing contact took the same name.
items.cn: 这件工具变成了动词，轻轻掠过的一触也沿用了同一个词。

items.en: Today brush covers the tool, the stroke, the light touch and the low bushes.
items.cn: 今天 brush 覆盖工具、刷的动作、轻擦与低矮灌木。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects tools and cleaning words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收工具与清洁相关的词。

entries.definition: To turn red in the face from shyness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「脸红」，拼写与 brush 相近。

entries.definition: To press something so hard that it breaks.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「压碎」，读音与 brush 接近。

entries.definition: To move very quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「冲；急速行进」，读音与 brush 接近。

entries.definition: A toothed tool for tidying hair.
To clean a floor with a long brush.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扫地」，用长柄刷清扫。

entries.definition: To rub something hard to clean it.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: A brush was once a bundle of twigs from a stiff shrub.
normal.cn: brush 最初是把一种硬枝灌木扎成的一束枝条。

normal.en: French brosse brought the word into English in the fourteenth century.
normal.cn: 法语 brosse 在十四世纪把这个词带进了英语。

normal.en: Because a brush stroke is light, brushing past someone means barely touching.
normal.cn: 因为刷一下很轻，所以 brush past 某人就是几乎没碰到。

normal.en: It often pairs with teeth, hair, paint and against.
normal.cn: 它常与 teeth、hair、paint、against 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-u-s-h; add -es for brushes and -ed for brushed.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-u-s-h；复数加 -es 成为 brushes，过去式加 -ed 成为 brushed。

abstract.en: See a bundle of stiff hairs tied to a wooden handle: that bundle is a brush.
abstract.cn: 想象一束硬毛绑在木柄上：这束东西就是 brush。

abstract.en: Make the hairs long and soft and the same tool paints a picture.
abstract.cn: 把毛变长变软，同一件工具就能画画。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the bundle of hairs bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那束毛把意思带回来。

examples.en: She dipped the brush in paint and began to draw.
examples.cn: 她把画笔蘸上颜料，开始作画。

examples.en: He brushes his teeth twice a day.
examples.cn: 他每天刷两次牙。

examples.en: Her sleeve brushed against my arm.
examples.cn: 她的袖子擦过我的手臂。

root: brush 来自古法语 brosse，可上溯到拉丁语 bruscus，那是一种枝条硬挺、常被扎起来擦洗的灌木。英语在十四世纪借入这个词，指清洁工具；后来这件工具又变成动词，表示刷、梳，也指轻轻掠过；同一个词还保留了「灌木丛」这个来自枝条的意思。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of brush grow from one picture: a bundle of stiff hairs tied to a handle.
sensesIntro.cn: brush 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：绑在柄上的一束硬毛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bundle of stiff hairs fixed to a wooden handle
core.cn: 核心意象：一束绑在木柄上的硬毛

branches.en: THE TOOL: the object itself is the first sense.
branches.cn: 工具线：这件器物本身是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE STROKE: the verb names what the tool does.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指这件工具所做的动作。

branches.en: THE GRAZE: a light stroke becomes any passing touch.
branches.cn: 轻擦线：轻轻一刷扩展为任何掠过的接触。

branches.en: THE SHRUB: the twigs that made brushes keep their own name.
branches.cn: 灌木线：扎刷子用的枝条保留了自己的名字。

branches.en: THE HAND: tool and stroke belong to the same hand.
branches.cn: 手线：工具与动作属于同一只手。

intro.en: Brush is a base noun and verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: brush 是基础名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bruscus is the shrub behind the French word; seta means a bristle and is a parallel term.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bruscus 是法语词背后的那种灌木，seta 意为「鬃毛」，属平行词。

items.meaning: a bundle of twigs, a brush
items.example: Brosse is the recorded French source.
items.exampleCN: brosse 是有记录的法语来源。

the hard parts in the mouth

definition_zh: 主意；想法；概念；意见
definition_en: a thought, plan or suggestion formed in the mind
core_image: 脑子里亮起的一盏小灯
scene: 会议室安静了很久。 Then he raised his hand and offered a new idea.
sceneCN: 这里 idea 是「主意」（第 1 个义项：脑中形成的计划或提议）；句意：他举手提出了一个新主意。

derivatives.zh: 理想；理想的；同根异位
理想主义；ideal 加后缀
构思；形成概念；动词化形式

senses.title: A plan or suggestion
senses.definition: a plan or suggestion offered in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情境中提出的计划或建议
senses.example: Her idea saved the school trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主意挽救了学校郊游。
senses.why: A lamp lights up in the head: something actionable appears.
senses.whyCN: 脑中亮起一盏灯：可付诸行动的东西出现了。

senses.title: A mental picture or concept
senses.definition: a thought or image held in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 心中持有的想法或图像
senses.example: The idea of freedom means different things to different people.
senses.exampleCN: 自由的概念因人而异。
senses.why: The light need not act; it can simply illuminate a notion.
senses.whyCN: 这盏灯不必行动，它也可以只照亮一个概念。

senses.title: Vague knowledge or belief
senses.definition: a rough knowledge or opinion about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的大致认识或看法
senses.example: I have no idea where the keys went.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全不知道钥匙去哪了。
senses.why: The mind holds a shadow of a thing: enough to guess, not enough to know.
senses.whyCN: 心中持有事物的影子：够猜测，不够确知。

senses.title: The aim or point of something
senses.definition: the purpose or point behind an action or design
senses.definitionCN: 行动或设计背后的目的
senses.example: The idea of the game is to work together.
senses.exampleCN: 这个游戏的本意是协作。
senses.why: The idea becomes the plan's inner intention, not a thought in a head.
senses.whyCN: idea 变成计划内在的意图，而非头脑中的念头。

senses.title: High conception in philosophy
senses.definition: in philosophy, a timeless archetype or perfect form
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中超越时间的原型或完美形式
senses.example: Plato placed eternal ideas above the world of things.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图把永恒理念置于万物之上。
senses.why: The everyday thought is raised to a perfect, eternal model.
senses.whyCN: 日常的想法被提升为完美永恒的范型。

intro.en: Idea comes from Greek idea, look or form, the verb idein, to see. Plato made it a technical term for eternal forms, and Latin and the European languages inherited it.
intro.cn: idea 源自希腊语 idea「外观、形式」，出自动词 idein「看」。柏拉图将其定为指永恒理念的术语，拉丁语及欧洲诸语言继承了它。

items.en: Greek idea meant form, pattern or look, from idein, to see; what is seen with the mind's eye.
items.cn: 希腊语 idea 意为形式、样式或外观，出自 idein「看」；即心灵之眼所见之物。

items.en: Plato used idea for the eternal, perfect models behind visible things.
items.cn: 柏拉图用 idea 指可见事物背后永恒完美的范型。

items.en: Latin borrowed idea as a learned word and kept it in philosophical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语将 idea 作为学术词借入，保存在哲学写作中。

items.en: Middle English took idea through Latin in the sixteenth century, first in Platonic contexts.
items.cn: 中古英语经拉丁语在十六世纪借入 idea，最初用于柏拉图式语境。

items.en: Modern English loosened the term until any thought or plan could be an idea.
items.cn: 现代英语放宽词义，任何想法或计划都可称 idea。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the idea family. The meaning group compares thought words from a quick spark to a formal concept.
note.cn: 形近组收录 idea 词族；词义组比较从灵光一闪到正式概念的思考用词。

entries.definition: a perfect model or standard; also, existing only in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 理想；理想的。同根的姊妹词。

entries.definition: a system of ideas behind politics or culture.
entries.definitionCN: 意识形态。理念的系统化。

entries.definition: an object of worship. Sounds close but comes from a Greek word for image in a religious sense.
entries.definitionCN: 偶像。发音相近，但出自希腊语「宗教形象」一词。

entries.definition: anything produced by thinking; broader than idea.
entries.definitionCN: 想法。范围比 idea 宽。

entries.definition: a vague or personal belief or concept.
an abstract general idea, often in academic use.
entries.definitionCN: 概念。偏抽象、常用于学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split idea into i + dea, play on the seeing root, and use the no idea phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 idea 拆成 i 加 dea，玩味「看」的词根，并用 no idea 短语。

normal.en: The root means to see: an idea is what your inner eye sees.
normal.cn: 词根意为「看」：idea 是心眼所见。

normal.en: no idea is the everyday negative: I have no idea at all.
normal.cn: no idea 是日常否定式：我毫无头绪。

normal.en: a bright idea is the lightbulb cartoon moment.
normal.cn: a bright idea 就是漫画里灯泡亮起的瞬间。

normal.en: ideal is idea plus al: the perfect version of a thought.
normal.cn: ideal 是 idea 加 al：想法的完美版。

normal.en: get ideas warns that someone is dreaming above their place.
normal.cn: get ideas 警示有人开始想入非非。

abstract.en: One image: a small lamp switching on in a dark head.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：黑暗的头颅里小灯亮起。

abstract.en: An idea is a seed: small, complete, ready to grow.
abstract.cn: idea 是种子：小而完整，随时可以生长。

abstract.en: From spark to system: idea, ideal, ideology.
abstract.cn: 从火花到体系：idea、ideal、ideology。

examples.en: That's a great idea; let's try it this weekend.
examples.cn: 这主意太好了，周末就试试。

examples.en: The idea behind the design is simplicity.
examples.cn: 这个设计背后的理念是简约。

examples.en: Nobody had any idea how hard the climb would be.
examples.cn: 没人知道这次攀登有多艰难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱地里挖」：好主意就像埋在地里的宝贝，爱到地里挖才挖得出来。

root: 希腊语 idea「形式、外观」（idein「看」），柏拉图用以指永恒理念；经拉丁语于十六世纪进入英语，现代英语放宽为任何想法、主意。

sensesIntro.en: Idea runs from a doable plan to a mental image, a vague belief, the inner purpose of a design, and finally the perfect forms of philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: idea 从可执行的主意到心中图像、模糊的印象、设计的本意，最终抵达哲学中的完美理念。

core.en: A light switched on inside the mind: something seen before it exists.
core.cn: 头脑里亮起的一盏灯：事物存在之前先被看见。

branches.en: PROPOSAL: an idea you can act on this afternoon.
branches.cn: 提议：下午就能动手的 idea。

branches.en: CONCEPT: the idea of freedom or justice.
branches.cn: 概念：自由或正义的 idea。

branches.en: IMPRESSION: no idea, half an idea.
branches.cn: 印象：毫无头绪或略知一二。

branches.en: PURPOSE: the idea of the game or of the law.
branches.cn: 本意：游戏或法律的 idea。

branches.en: PLATONIC FORM: ideas as eternal models.
branches.cn: 柏拉图式理念：作为永恒范型的 ideas。

intro.en: Idea spawns ideal, ideology and ideate, all keeping the seeing root inside.
intro.cn: idea 派生出 ideal、ideology、ideate，都保留着「看」的词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the borrowed philosophical noun as it passed into learned European use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示这个借入的哲学名词如何进入欧洲学术用法。

items.example: She turned a rough idea into a business.
items.exampleCN: 她把粗略的想法做成了生意。

items.example: The resort matched their ideal of a holiday.
items.exampleCN: 这个度假村符合他们对假期的理想。

items.example: The party's ideology shaped its policies.
items.exampleCN: 该党的意识形态塑造了其政策。
设计师先构思再画草图。

items.example: His idealism outlasted the hard years.
items.exampleCN: 他的理想主义熬过了艰难岁月。

items.example: The committee sat idealess for hours.

definition_zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
definition_en: the reason for which something is done, made or exists
core_image: 木匠在工作台上把一块木板摆正，用粉线弹出一条笔直的线，才落下第一锯
scene: 开工之前，工头把图纸摊在木板上，用手指按住那条基准线，说明这块料为什么要留厚两毫米。 The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
sceneCN: 这里 purpose 指「做某件事所依据的目的」（第 1 个义项：意图与目的）；句意为多留那两毫米是为了还能再刨一次。图中可辨识物件：摊开的图纸、按住基准线的手指、弹过粉线的木板、留下的余量；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「有明确目的的」
由名词加副词后缀构成，语义由「意图」转为「故意地」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「没有目的的」
由名词与过去分词复合而成，语义由「用途」转为「专为某用途建造的」
加表示「多」的前缀构成，语义由「用途」转为「一物多用的」

senses.title: The reason for an act
senses.titleCN: 做一件事的理由与意图
senses.definition: the reason one has in mind for doing something or for making something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事或造某物时心里所抱的理由
senses.example: The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
senses.exampleCN: 多留那两毫米，是为了还能再刨一次。
senses.why: the word comes from putting something forward, so a purpose is the aim a person sets in front of the work before starting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自「把某物摆到前面」，因此目的就是开工前把目标摆在工作前面的那件事。

senses.title: The function of a thing
senses.definition: the job that an object or a part is designed to perform
senses.definitionCN: 一件物件或部件被造出来所要承担的功能
senses.example: This room has outlived its original purpose as a laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子原本用作洗衣房，如今那个用途早已过去了。
senses.why: the aim moves from the maker's head into the made thing, where it becomes a function.
senses.whyCN: 目标从造物者的脑子里移到被造之物里，在那里它就成了一种功能。

senses.title: Firmness of intention
senses.definition: resolute determination to carry out what one has decided
senses.definitionCN: 把已经决定的事做到底的那份坚决
senses.example: He spoke with purpose and nobody interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话带着决心，没人打断。
senses.why: a settled intention shows in the manner of speech, and the noun then names the firmness rather than the aim.
senses.whyCN: 已定的意图会显现在说话的方式上，此时名词指的是那份坚定，而不是目标。

senses.title: Relevance to the matter
senses.definition: the quality of bearing on the question at hand, as in remarks that are to the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与眼前问题相干的品质，如「切题」的话
senses.example: Every question was to the purpose, and the meeting ended early.
senses.exampleCN: 每个问题都切中正题，会议提前结束。
senses.why: what is aimed at the matter in hand is relevant, so a fixed phrase marks this older, narrower sense.
senses.whyCN: 对准眼前事务的就是相关的，因此一个固定说法保存了这条更窄的旧义。

senses.title: Meaning in a life
senses.definition: the sense that one's existence or work has a point worth serving
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己的存在或工作有一个值得效力的要点
senses.example: Teaching gave her a purpose she had not found in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 教书给了她一种在实验室里没找到的意义。
senses.why: when the aim is large enough to organize a life, the word shifts from a task to a reason for living.
senses.whyCN: 当目标大到足以组织一生，这个词就从一项任务转为活着的理由。

senses.title: A stated aim of an institution
senses.definition: the declared aim that a body, a fund or a law is set up to serve
senses.definitionCN: 一个机构、基金或法律被设立时所声明的目标
senses.example: The fund's purpose is written on its first page.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金的宗旨写在第一页上。
senses.why: organizations must put their aim forward in writing, which keeps the original image of placing something in front.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须把目标写在前面，这保留了「把某物摆到前面」的原初意象。

senses.title: Result actually achieved
senses.definition: the outcome that an action actually produces, as in efforts that came to good purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一个行动实际产生的效果，如「见了效」的努力
senses.example: All the digging came to good purpose when the well struck water.
senses.exampleCN: 井里出水时，所有挖掘都见了效。
senses.why: an aim that is realized becomes a result, and older English used the noun for that realized effect.
senses.whyCN: 实现的目标会变成结果，旧时英语就用这个名词指那种已实现的效用。

senses.title: A proposal or intent
senses.definition: a plan or proposal one puts forward, the sense closest to the French source
senses.definitionCN: 一个人摆出来的计划或提议，是最贴近法语来源的一层
senses.example: Their purpose was to rebuild the mill before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的打算是在入冬前把磨坊重建起来。
senses.why: the French ancestor meant a proposal put forward, and this plain sense still surfaces in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语祖词意为「摆出来的提议」，这一朴素义仍会在正式文字中浮现。

intro.en: Purpose comes through Old French porpos 'aim, intention' from porposer 'to put forth', a variant of proposer, which rests on Latin proponere 'to put forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ponere 'to place'. The deeper origin of ponere is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 porpos「目标、意图」来自 porposer「摆出、提出」，那是 proposer 的变体，其源头是拉丁 proponere「放到前面」，由 pro-「向前」与 ponere「放置」构成。ponere 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the proposal that links it to a root for 'to place' is circular and adds nothing, so the source is best left open.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。其更深来源不确定；把它与另一个同样表示「放置」的词根相联系只是循环解释，并无增益，因此来源宜存疑。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ponere gave proponere 'to put forward, set before one', used of plans, terms and proposals.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ponere 构成 proponere「摆到前面、置于眼前」，用于计划、条款与提议。

items.en: Old French porposer 'to put forth, intend' produced the noun porpos, which named both the aim and the resolve behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 porposer「提出、打算」产生名词 porpos，兼指目标与背后的决心。

items.en: Middle English took purpose for an intention, and the phrase on purpose later fixed the sense of doing something deliberately.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词表示意图，后来固定说法「故意地」把「有意为之」的意思定了下来。

items.en: Modern law and administration use the noun for the declared aim of a body, which is the oldest image of putting an aim in front of the work.
items.cn: 现代法律与行政用这个名词指机构声明的宗旨，这正是「把目标摆在工作前面」最古老的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ponere and the exact date of the deliberateness phrase): no citation fixes the first use for an institution's aim, and any Indo-European form offered for ponere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ponere 的更深来源与「故意」说法确切成形的年代）：机构宗旨义没有确切的最早书证；凡为 ponere 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates verbs and nouns built on the same placing root; group two separates words for an aim by how explicit it is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「放置」词根的动词与名词；第二组按明确程度区分表示「目标」的词。

entries.definition: The direct relative: to put a plan or an offer before others, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 最直接的同族词：把计划或提议摆到别人面前，同出那个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From the same placing verb through French: to put something forward, hence to set a question or hold a position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「放置」动词经法语而来：把某物摆出，因而指提出问题或摆出姿势。

entries.definition: In- 'upon' plus ponere: to place a burden on someone, which is the same root pressing downward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「在上」加 ponere 构成：把负担压在别人身上，同一词根往下用力。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: to put parts together, hence to write or to calm oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 ponere 构成：把部件放到一起，因而指写作或使镇定。

entries.definition: From pro- plus portare 'to carry': to carry a meaning or a claim, with no placing involved and no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pro- 加 portare「搬运」构成：承载某种含义或声称，不含「放置」，也不同根。

entries.definition: The thing one intends to hit or reach; it is sharper and more specific than purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 打算击中或抵达的东西；比 purpose 更尖锐、更具体。

entries.definition: A defined end point one can mark and check; purpose is broader and can be a reason rather than a finish line.
entries.definitionCN: 一个可标示、可核对的明确终点；purpose 更宽，可以是理由而非终点线。

entries.definition: What a person means to do, often before acting; it is closer to the mental state than to the thing served.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算做什么，多在行动之前；更接近心理状态，而不是所服务的事。

entries.definition: The explanation of why something is as it is; it can look backward, while purpose looks forward.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某事为何如此的理由；可以向后看，而 purpose 向前看。

entries.definition: The work a thing performs; it is the mechanical face of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所执行的工作；是 purpose 在机械层面的面孔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means to place, and the prefix means forward: a purpose is an aim placed in front of the work.
normal.cn: 词根意为「放置」，前缀意为「向前」：目的就是被摆在工作前面的那个目标。

normal.en: The family runs purpose, purposeful, purposely, purposeless, purpose-built, multipurpose.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、形容词、副词、否定式与两个复合词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: on purpose, serve a purpose, fit for purpose, a sense of purpose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：故意地、起作用、适合用途、目标感。

normal.en: The siblings propose, pose, impose and compose all come from the same placing verb.
normal.cn: 同族的 propose、pose、impose 与 compose 都出自那个「放置」动词。

normal.en: The look-alike purport comes from a verb meaning to carry, so it means to claim rather than to intend.
normal.cn: 形近的 purport 出自一个意为「搬运」的动词，所以它的意思是「声称」而非「打算」。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line snapped on a board before the first cut.
abstract.cn: 想象第一锯之前，木板上先弹出的一条粉线。

abstract.en: Picture a sign at the head of a path saying what the path is for.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小路的起点立着一块牌子，写着这条路是为什么修的。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp aimed at one desk rather than lighting the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照一张桌子，而不是照亮整间屋子。

examples.en: The purpose of the new rule is to slow the traffic at the gate.
examples.cn: 新规定的目的是让门口的车辆慢下来。

examples.en: He knocked the cup over on purpose and then apologized.
examples.cn: 他故意碰倒杯子，然后又道了歉。

examples.en: The building has served its purpose and will be pulled down.
examples.cn: 这座楼已经完成它的用途，将被拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「purpose 破的」——先想清楚为什么做，才不容易把事情做破 → 目的

root: 古法语 porpos「目标、意图」← porposer「提出」← 拉丁 proponere「放到前面」= pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）；ponere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: an aim is placed in front of the work, and that placed aim then becomes a function, a firmness, a relevance, a reason for living, an institutional charter, a realized effect and finally a plain proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先把目标摆到工作前面，这个被摆出的目标随后变成一项功能、一份坚定、一种相关性、一个活着的理由、一纸机构宗旨、一个已实现的效果，最后成为一句朴素的提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snapped chalk line laid on a board before the saw goes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：锯子落下之前，先在被板上弹出一条粉线。

branches.en: THE AIM PUT FORWARD: an intention in the mind and a proposal spoken aloud.
branches.cn: 摆出的目标：心里的意图与说出口的提议。

branches.en: THE AIM BUILT IN: one aim settles into a thing's function, another into a body's charter.
branches.cn: 被造进去的目标：一个目标落成物的功能，另一个落成机构的宗旨。

branches.en: THE AIM HELD TIGHT: resolve is the same aim felt as will.
branches.cn: 被握紧的目标：决心就是同一个目标在意志层面的感受。

branches.en: AIMED AND REALIZED: what bears on the matter, and what actually comes of it.
branches.cn: 对准与实现：切中事务的，以及确实做出来的效果。

branches.en: AIM LARGE ENOUGH FOR A LIFE: the aim becomes a reason to get up.
branches.cn: 大到足够撑起一生的目标：目标变成起床的理由。

intro.en: Purpose is a French-shaped noun whose Latin prefix and verb are still productive in English, so its parts can be read clearly.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态的名词，其拉丁前缀与动词在英语里仍有构成力，因此部件读得很清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' gives propose, impose, compose, position and deposit; pro- 'forward' appears in proceed, promote and protect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere「放置」衍生出 propose、impose、compose、position 与 deposit；pro-「向前」见于 proceed、promote 与 protect。

items.example: The prefix puts the aim ahead of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目标放在行动之前。
这个词根提供「放置」的动作。

items.example: The plan was put forward at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 计划在会上被提了出来。

items.example: The purpose was written on the first page.
A purposeful walk covered the ridge by noon.
items.exampleCN: 一次有目的的行走在正午前走完了山脊。

items.example: She purposely left the door open.

items.exampleCN: 没有目的的挖掘毁了草坪。

items.example: A purpose-built studio replaced the shed.
items.exampleCN: 一间专用工作室取代了棚屋。

items.example: A multipurpose hall serves the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 一座多用途大厅供全村使用。
他们提出了一条更短的路线。

definition_zh: 伟大的；重大的；好极了；大量的
definition_en: very large in size or degree, very good, or important in rank or history
core_image: 被放大到顶的量：大到让人抬头看，好到让人叫出声
scene: 运动场边的人群起立欢呼，把帽子抛向空中。 The great wall stretched far beyond the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 great 是「巨大的、伟大的」（第 1 个义项：规模或程度极大）；句意为那道巨墙绵延远超群山。

pos.zh: 形容词：大的；大量的；伟大的；极好的
副词（口语）：很好地；大大地（greatly 的口语形）
名词（复数）：大人物；杰出人物

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀，义为「大大地；非常」
加名词后缀，义为「伟大；巨大」
与 large 同族的相关词，义为「扩大」

senses.title: Unusually large in size or amount
senses.definition: very big in size, number, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或程度上非常大
senses.example: A great crowd gathered in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群人聚集在广场上。
senses.why: The core image is quantity pushed to the top, so size comes first.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把数量推到顶，所以体量义最先出现。

senses.title: Very good or enjoyable
senses.definition: very good, pleasant, or enjoyable
senses.definitionCN: 非常好、令人愉快
senses.example: The concert was great from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会从头到尾都棒极了。
senses.why: What is large impresses, and what impresses is praised.
senses.whyCN: 大到令人惊叹，惊叹便化为称赞，于是有了夸赞义。

senses.title: Important or famous
senses.definition: important, powerful, or famous in history or society
senses.definitionCN: 在历史或社会中重要、有影响
senses.example: She is one of the great scientists of this age.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这个时代最伟大的科学家之一。
senses.why: Large size moves up to large reputation.
senses.whyCN: 体量之大升格为声名之大。

senses.title: One generation further up or down
senses.definition: used in family words to add one more generation, as in great-grandfather
senses.definitionCN: 用于亲属词再加一代，如 great-grandfather
senses.example: Her great grandmother lived through the old century.
senses.exampleCN: 她的曾祖母经历过上个世纪。
senses.why: Grand already means one step; great stacks one more step.
senses.whyCN: grand 已表隔一代，great 再叠一步，故成隔两代。

intro.en: Great is a native word for big that outgrew every synonym.
intro.cn: great 是本族的「大」，后来盖过了所有同义词。

items.en: A Germanic adjective family for coarse and thick underlies the word.
items.cn: 词的基础是日耳曼语中形容粗厚的形容词族。

items.en: Old English great meant thick, coarse, or large.
items.cn: 古英语 great 意为粗的、厚的、大的。

items.en: Great displaced mickle as the everyday word for big.
items.cn: 中古英语中 great 取代 mickle 成为日常「大」字。

items.en: The praise sense and kinship use flourished in modern speech.
items.cn: 现代英语中夸赞义与亲属用法繁荣起来。

items.en: Daily speech keeps raising the bar for great.
items.cn: 日常口语不断提升 great 的使用频率。

note.en: Great, big and large divide the work of saying large.
note.cn: great、big、large 分工表达「大」。

entries.definition: to say hello; one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 问候；与 great 仅差一个字母

entries.definition: the quality of being great
animal fat; sounds alike, unrelated
the plain everyday word for large
formal and measurable largeness
extremely large, beyond normal

normalIntro.en: Five hooks to make great feel great.
normalIntro.cn: 五条钩子让 great 感觉真的很棒。

normal.en: Great is big that learned to impress.
normal.cn: great 是学会了令人惊叹的 big。

normal.en: Great grandfather adds one generation beyond grand.
normal.cn: great grandfather 比 grand 再多一代。

normal.en: A great deal of means a big pile of.
normal.cn: a great deal of 就是一大堆。

normal.en: Great minds think alike, says the proverb.
normal.cn: 谚语说英雄所见略同。

normal.en: Kids say great for anything they love.
normal.cn: 孩子把喜欢的一切都称作 great。

abstract.en: Great is a shout stretched as long as the sound itself.
abstract.cn: great 是一声被拉长的欢呼。

abstract.en: Picture the tallest figure in the family photo.
abstract.cn: 想象全家福里最高的那个人影。

abstract.en: Every great thing once started merely big.
abstract.cn: 每个伟大的东西最初只是大。

examples.en: That was a great match last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚那场比赛太精彩了。

examples.en: It took a great deal of patience to finish.
examples.cn: 完成它需要极大的耐心。

examples.en: My great grandmother told us about the old days.
examples.cn: 我曾祖母给我们讲过去的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「古瑞特」——古往今来最瑞最特别的就是伟大；great 就是那个被仰视的「大」

root: 日耳曼本土词，古英语 great（粗、厚、大），与荷兰语 grate、德语 grob 相关；一般认为与表示「粗大」的印欧词根有关，无拉丁亲缘。

sensesIntro.en: From thick largeness to praise, fame and family generations.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从粗大出发，长出夸赞、伟大与隔两代亲属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: size pushed until people look up
core.cn: 核心意象：大到让人抬头看

branches.en: the huge amount
branches.cn: 巨大的量

branches.en: the shout of praise
branches.cn: 夸赞的欢呼

branches.en: the name history remembers

branches.cn: 再叠一代

intro.en: Great builds a wide family inside English itself.
intro.cn: great 在英语内部构成了庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relatives; the family is homegrown.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词；词族是本土长成的。

items.example: Old great meant coarse cloth too.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 great 也指粗布。

definition_zh: 没有人；谁都不；小人物；无名之辈
definition_en: not a single person, and also a person of no importance or influence
core_image: 一间本该坐满人的屋子，椅子全是空的
scene: 会议室的门开着，桌上的杯子还冒着热气，可一圈椅子全是空的。 Nobody came to the meeting, so the chairs stayed empty all afternoon.

senses.title: Not a single person
senses.definition: not one person; no person at all, used when the number of people present is zero
senses.definitionCN: 一个人也没有；表示在场人数为零
senses.example: Nobody was waiting at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站里没有一个人在等。
senses.why: The word welds the negator no onto body, so it denies not an action but the very existence of a human figure in the scene.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把否定词 no 焊在 body 上，否定的不是某个动作，而是场景里是否存在一个具体的人。

senses.title: A person of no importance
senses.definition: an ordinary or unimportant person, especially one without fame or influence
senses.definitionCN: 普通而不重要的人，尤指没有名声或影响力的人
senses.example: He was a nobody before the film made him famous.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部电影让他出名之前，他只是个无名小卒。
senses.why: Once nobody rules out any important figure, the phrase can be turned into a countable noun that names the missing importance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当 nobody 排除了任何重要人物之后，这个说法就能变成可数名词，直接指那份缺失的分量。

senses.title: No person except
senses.definition: used in the pattern nobody but to mean no person other than the one named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 nobody but 结构，表示除了提到的这个人之外没有别人
senses.example: Nobody but the guard saw him leave.
senses.exampleCN: 除了门卫，没有人看见他离开。
senses.why: The negator still empties the scene of people, and but then names the single exception hidden inside that emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 否定词仍然把场景里的人清空，but 随后点出藏在这片空无之中的唯一例外。

intro.en: Nobody is an English compound of the negator no and the noun body, first recorded in the fourteenth century and not borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nobody 是英语否定词 no 与名词 body 的复合，最早见于十四世纪，并非借自拉丁语。

items.en: The Old English negator nā meant not or no, and it is the ancestor of modern no.
items.cn: 古英语否定词 nā 意为「不、没有」，是现代 no 的前身。

items.en: Bodig meant the body, the physical frame of a person, and became modern body.
items.cn: bodig 指身体、人的躯体，后来演变为 body。

items.en: In the fourteenth century the two words were joined as nobody, a pronoun meaning no person.
items.cn: 十四世纪这两个词合成 nobody，作代词表示「没有人」。

items.en: Writers began using a nobody as a countable noun for a person of no account.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作家开始用 a nobody 这个可数名词，指无足轻重的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps both uses and adds the plural nobodies for several unimportant people.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两种用法，并加上复数 nobodies 来指多个无足轻重的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pronouns built from the same body element; the near-meaning group gathers words for absence of people and for insignificance.
note.cn: 形近组收以同一个 body 成分构成的一组代词；近义组收表示「没有人」以及「无足轻重」的词。

entries.definition: Some person; the positive counterpart built on body.

intro.en: Rule comes from Latin regula, a straight stick or standard.
intro.cn: rule 源自拉丁语 regula，意为直尺或标准。

items.en: Regula means a straight stick.
items.cn: regula 意为笔直的杆或尺。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导、使笔直。

items.en: Riule means a rule or order.
items.cn: riu le 意为规则或命令。

items.en: Rule covers standards and government.
items.cn: rule 兼指标准与统治。

items.en: Rule also means to give a decision.
items.cn: rule 还表示作出裁定。

note.en: A rule is a standard; a ruse is a trick.

normalIntro.en: A rule draws a line and keeps people inside it.
normalIntro.cn: rule 划出一条界线，把人约束在其中。

normal.en: The club has a rule against smoking.
normal.cn: 俱乐部有禁止吸烟的规定。

normal.en: The emperor ruled the land for many years.
normal.cn: 皇帝统治这片土地多年。

normal.en: The court ruled that the arrest was illegal.
normal.cn: 法院裁定这次逮捕不合法。

normal.en: As a rule, she walks to work.
normal.cn: 通常她步行上班。

normal.en: Doctors ruled out a broken bone.
normal.cn: 医生排除了骨折的可能。

abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子画出一条笔直的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown placed over a map.

abstract.en: Think of a judge's hammer setting a boundary.

examples.cn: 委员会裁定该计划可以继续。

root: 拉丁语 regula（直尺、标准）来自 regere（使笔直、引导），核心义「划出直线、立下标准」，再引申为统治与裁定。

branches.cn: 控制变成表示统治的动词。

definition_zh: 相对的；相关的；亲戚
definition_en: true only when compared with something else; connected with a particular subject; a member of one's family
core_image: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高
scene: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上，看起来竟一样高。 Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
sceneCN: 这里 relative 是「相对的」（第 1 个义项：只有在比较中才成立）；句意为幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。画面里可留意：不同高度的台阶、看起来一样高的两人。

derivatives.zh: 相对地；相当地
相对性；相对论
关系；亲属

senses.title: True only by comparison
senses.definition: not absolute, but true when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 非绝对的，只有在与其他事物比较时才成立
senses.example: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。
senses.why: The Latin participle means carried back, and a value carried back to another value is measured by it rather than in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁分词意为「被带回的」，一个数值被带回另一个数值那里，就是以它为准来衡量，而不是就自身而言。

senses.title: Connected with a subject
senses.definition: having a connection with a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某个特定事项有关联
senses.example: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。
senses.why: Something carried back to a question is relevant to it, and the same adjective names that connection.
senses.whyCN: 被带回到某个问题那里的东西就与它有关，同一个形容词命名这种关联。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: A distant relative left her the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。
senses.why: Persons related by blood are quite literally carried back to a common ancestor, and the adjective became a noun for them.
senses.whyCN: 有血缘的人确实可以被带回同一个祖先，于是这个形容词就成了指他们的名词。

intro.en: Relative is the adjective of the Latin participle carried back; what is carried back is measured against something else, or joined to a family.
intro.cn: relative 是拉丁分词「被带回的」所对应的形容词；被带回的东西，要么以别物为尺，要么归入一个家族。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, the root of referre and of the whole rel- family.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带，是 referre 与整个 rel- 词族的根。

items.en: Relatus, the participle of referre, meant carried back or having reference to.
items.cn: relatus 是 referre 的分词，意为被带回的或有所指的。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else, the grammatical and philosophical term.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的，是语法与哲学术语。

items.en: English used the adjective for values that hold only in comparison, as opposed to absolute ones.
items.cn: 英语用这个形容词表示只在比较中成立的数值，与「绝对」相对。

items.en: The noun use for a family member grew from the sense of persons referred to one another by blood.
items.cn: 指亲属的名词用法，由「因血缘而彼此相关的人」这一意义发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of comparison and kinship words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词干的词；近义组收表比较的形容词与亲属词。

normalIntro.en: The word means carried back to something else: a value to another value, a fact to a question, a person to a family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「被带回别处」：数值带回另一数值，事实带回一个问题，人带回一个家族。

normal.en: Relative to means measured against.
normal.cn: relative to 意为以……为参照来衡量。

normal.en: Relative humidity compares moisture with the maximum the air can hold.
normal.cn: relative humidity 把湿度与空气能容纳的最大量相比。

normal.en: A close relative is a near member of the family.
normal.cn: a close relative 是家族中的近亲。

normal.en: Relative importance ranks things against each other.
normal.cn: relative importance 是把事物相互比较后的轻重。

normal.en: Relative and absolute are a pair; one needs the other.
normal.cn: relative 与 absolute 是一对，彼此需要。

abstract.en: Almost everything we call large is only relatively large.
abstract.cn: 我们所说的大，几乎都只是相对地大。

abstract.en: To see things as relative is not to see them as unreal.
abstract.cn: 把事物看作相对的，并不等于把它们看作虚幻的。

abstract.en: A family is the first place where a person is a relative.
abstract.cn: 家庭是一个人最初成为「亲属」的地方。

examples.en: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
examples.cn: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。

examples.en: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（带回、关联）加 ive：必须带回别物才有意义，是相对；与某个问题带回一处，是相关；因血缘被带回一家，是亲戚。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative；同族有 relatively、relativity、relation、relate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is carried back to something else; the senses move from a value measured by comparison, to a fact tied to a subject, to a person tied to a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被带回别物那里」；义项从以比较为准的数值，到与某个主题相连的事实，再到与家族相连的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on steps of different heights, looking the same size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高。

branches.en: two figures that only make sense together
branches.cn: 只有放在一起才有意义的两个数字

branches.en: facts gathered around one accident

branches.cn: 一位远亲留下的老房子

branches.cn: 一次比较与一次对主题的指向

branches.en: tied to a question and tied to a family
branches.cn: 与一个问题相连，与一个家族相连

intro.en: The participle carried back becomes an adjective of comparison, and the adjective then becomes a noun for a family member.
intro.cn: 「被带回的」分词变成表比较的形容词，这个形容词又变成指亲属的名词。

definition_zh: 她自己；她亲自
definition_en: the reflexive form of she, used when the object is the same female person as the subject
core_image: 动作绕一圈回到她自己的手上
scene: 妹妹坚持不用帮忙，独自把散落的拼图一块块拼好，晚饭前完成了整幅作品。 The little girl completed the big puzzle all by herself before dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 herself 是「她自己；她亲自」（第 1 个义项：反身用法）；拼图由她独立完成，动作回到自身。

derivatives.zh: 阳性对应反身代词，义为「他自己」
第一人称对应反身代词，义为「我自己」
复数对应反身代词，义为「他们自己」

senses.title: Reflexive: object equals subject
senses.definition: used when the female subject and the object of the verb are the same person
senses.definitionCN: 主语与宾语为同一位女性时使用
senses.example: She looked at herself in the old mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 她照了照那面旧镜子。
senses.why: The action bends back onto the doer, so the word mirrors she.
senses.whyCN: 动作弯回施动者本人，所以这个词是 she 的「镜子」。

senses.title: Emphatic: she did it personally
senses.definition: used to stress that the female person did it personally
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事由她本人亲自完成
senses.example: The head teacher herself welcomed the new pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 校长亲自迎接了新生。
senses.why: Putting herself next to the noun singles that person out.
senses.whyCN: 把 herself 放在名词旁就把这个人单独点亮。

intro.en: Herself compounds her with the old word self.
intro.cn: herself 由 her 与古老的 self 复合而成。

items.en: Old English used hire selfum, meaning to her own self.
items.cn: 古英语有 hire selfum，意为「对她自己」。

items.en: The element self long expressed one's own person in Germanic.
items.cn: self 元素在日耳曼语中长期表「自身」。

items.en: Middle English fused the pair into the single form herself.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者融合为 herself 一词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both reflexive and emphatic uses.
items.cn: 现代英语兼有反身与强调两种用法。

items.en: The reflexive family grew in parallel: myself, himself, themselves.
items.cn: 反身代词家族同步壮大：myself、himself、themselves。

note.en: Compare herself with the reflexive family.
note.cn: 把 herself 与反身代词家族对照。

normal.en: Every pronoun has its self, one per person.

abstract.en: Picture a boomerang returning to the girl's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象回旋镖飞回女孩手中——反身的画面。

abstract.en: Feel the mirror: the doer and receiver are one person.
abstract.cn: 感受镜子：做者与受者是同一人。

abstract.en: See a spotlight jump onto her when herself appears.
abstract.cn: herself 一出现，聚光灯就打到她身上。

examples.en: She made the birthday cake herself last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚的生日蛋糕是她亲手做的。

examples.en: The girl taught herself to swim in one summer.
examples.cn: 那个女孩一个夏天就自学了游泳。

examples.en: Mary herself will host the class meeting.
examples.cn: 玛丽将亲自主持班会。

sensesIntro.en: Herself bends actions back to the doer or lifts her out of the crowd.

definition_zh: 交流；通信；沟通；传达；交通联系
definition_en: the act of sharing information, ideas or feelings; ways of sending messages
core_image: 消息在人与人之间往返的小路
scene: 班会课上，大家讨论怎样让班级消息传得更快。 Good communication makes our class run smoothly.
sceneCN: 这里 communication 是「沟通」（第 1 个义项：分享信息的行为）；句意是良好的沟通让班级运转顺畅。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「交流；沟通」
由 communicate 加 -ive 构成，义为「善于沟通的」
由 communicate 加 -or 构成，义为「沟通者」

senses.title: The act of sharing information
senses.definition: the process of giving and receiving messages
senses.definitionCN: 发送与接收信息的过程
senses.example: Communication between teachers and parents helps students.
senses.exampleCN: 家校沟通对学生有帮助。
senses.why: Two minds join when messages travel both ways.
senses.whyCN: 消息双向流动，两颗心便连在一起。

senses.title: Ways of sending messages
senses.definition: systems such as phone, post and internet
senses.definitionCN: 电话、邮政、互联网等系统
senses.example: Modern communication makes the world smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 现代通信让世界变小。
senses.why: Each new tool widens the road for messages.
senses.whyCN: 每一种新工具都为消息拓宽道路。

senses.title: Connections between places

senses.definitionCN: 连接各地的道路、铁路或航线
senses.example: The valley's communication with town is a narrow road.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷与城镇之间只有一条窄路相连。
senses.why: Places that share a road can share everything else.
senses.whyCN: 有路相连的地方，万事都可互通。

items.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为共同的。

items.cn: 它最初指共享事物与圣餐礼。

latinIntro.en: Latin communicatio passed through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communicatio 经法语进入英语。

items.example: Municipal means of a town's public service.
Communication is the act of sharing.
A communicative child makes friends easily.
items.exampleCN: 善于沟通的孩子容易交朋友。

items.example: Mass communication includes TV and radio.

definition_zh: 音乐家；乐手；演奏者；有音乐才华的人
definition_en: a person who plays, writes or performs music, whether as a profession or as a gift
core_image: 一个人坐在琴凳上，手指在琴键上找到下一个音
scene: 地铁通道人来人往，一个抱着吉他的年轻人靠墙站着，脚边是敞开的琴盒。 The musician played for the commuters and never once looked up.
sceneCN: 这里是「乐手、演奏者」（第 2 个义项：在乐队或公共场合演奏的人）；句意为那位乐手为来往的通勤者演奏，始终没有抬头。

derivatives.zh: 由 musician 加 -ship 构成，义为「音乐修养；演奏水准」
由 music 加 -al 构成，与 musician 同出 music，并非由 musician 加后缀而来
musician 由 music 加表示「从事某事的人」的 -ian 构成，因此 music 是它的基干，义为「音乐」

senses.title: Someone who makes music as a profession
senses.definition: a person who plays an instrument or writes music as a job, usually trained and paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 以演奏乐器或创作音乐为职业、通常受过训练并因此获得报酬的人
senses.example: He spent thirty years as a musician in the city orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 他在市立管弦乐团当了三十年音乐家。
senses.why: The suffix -ian marks a person who practises an art, as in historian and librarian, so musician is simply the person slot of the music family.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ian 标记从事某门技艺的人，historian、librarian 都是如此，所以 musician 就是「音乐」这一族词里指人的那个位置。

senses.title: A player within a band or orchestra
senses.definition: one of the players in a group, named by the part or instrument they take rather than by fame
senses.definitionCN: 乐队或乐团里的成员，按其声部或乐器来称呼，而不论名气
senses.example: The band's musicians tuned up before the doors opened.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队的乐手们在开门前调好了音。
senses.why: A group needs named roles, so the same word narrows to the players on stage, each holding one instrument and covering one part.
senses.whyCN: 一个团体需要有名有姓的分工，于是同一个词收窄为台上的演奏者，每人持一件乐器、负责一个声部。

senses.title: Someone with a gift for music, paid or not
senses.definition: a person unusually good at music, whether or not it is their job
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐上格外出色的人，不论是否以此为业
senses.example: My grandmother was a fine musician and played at every family wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖母是一位出色的音乐人，家里每场婚礼她都演奏。
senses.why: Because the word names ability as well as employment, it can praise an amateur whose playing is good enough to deserve the title.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指职业也指能力，所以也能用来称赞一位演奏水平够得上这个称号的业余爱好者。

intro.en: Musician names the person of the music family; English built it with -ian on the model of the Old French person noun.
intro.cn: musician 是「音乐」这一族词里指人的那个；英语仿照古法语的指人名词，用 -ian 把它构成。

items.en: The Greek noun mousike named the art of the Muses, and a person devoted to that art was already called mousikos.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 mousikē 指缪斯的技艺，献身于这门技艺的人当时就被称作 mousikos。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art, while musicus could serve both as an adjective and as a name for a musician.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术，而 musicus 既能作形容词，也能直接指乐师。

items.en: Old French musique named the art and became the base for a separate word for the person who practises it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 指这门艺术，并成为另一个指「从事此艺者」的词的基础。

items.en: Musicien added -ien to musique and named the player or writer of music, the form English met in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: musicien 在 musique 后加 -ien，指演奏或创作音乐的人，英语在十四世纪接触到这个词形。

items.en: English kept the stem and put its own -ian in place of -ien, giving musician, the spelling and ending used ever since.
items.cn: 英语保留词干，把本族惯用的 -ian 换进 -ien 的位置，得到 musician，这个拼写与词尾沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the nouns and adverbs of the same family; the near-meaning group collects the roles inside the music trade.
note.cn: 形近组收同一族里的名词与副词；近义组收音乐行业内部的不同角色。

entries.definition: The base noun of the family, naming the art itself.
entries.definitionCN: 这一族词的基干名词，指艺术本身。

entries.definition: The adjective from the same base, built with -al instead of -ian.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词，用 -al 而非 -ian 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a musical way, built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以音乐的方式」的副词，由 musical 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Musician plus -ship, naming the skill rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: musician 加 -ship，指技艺而不是人。

entries.definition: Someone who plays or sings in front of an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前演奏或演唱的人。

entries.definition: A person who writes music rather than only playing it.
entries.definitionCN: 写音乐而不只是演奏的人。

entries.definition: A musician who plays an instrument rather than sings.
entries.definitionCN: 演奏乐器而非演唱的音乐人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the person slot of the music family, and the suffixes around it show skill, art and base.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「音乐」这一族词里指人的位置，周围的后缀分别标出技艺、艺术与基干。

normal.en: Musician is music plus -ian, the same suffix that makes historian and librarian into people.
normal.cn: musician 是 music 加 -ian，同一个后缀也把 historian、librarian 变成指人的词。

normal.en: The Old French original was musicien; English kept the stem and swapped the ending for its own -ian.
normal.cn: 古法语原形是 musicien，英语保留词干，把词尾换成本族惯用的 -ian。

normal.en: Musicianship is musician plus -ship, naming the skill rather than the person who has it.
normal.cn: musicianship 是 musician 加 -ship，指技艺而不是拥有技艺的人。

normal.en: A street musician is a fixed phrase for someone who plays in public for coins and attention.
normal.cn: street musician 是固定说法，指在公共场所演奏、靠路人投币与围观为生的人。

normal.en: A session musician is hired for a single recording or tour, which shows the word covers many kinds of paid work.
normal.cn: session musician 指只为一次录音或巡演受雇的乐师，说明这个词覆盖多种有偿工作。

abstract.en: Behind every musician stands a long room of scales that nobody ever clapped for.
abstract.cn: 每位音乐家背后都有一间长长的琴房，里面是无人喝彩的音阶。

abstract.en: The word moves easily between a star on a poster and a neighbour with a guitar, because ability is the real test.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易地从海报上的明星滑到隔壁抱吉他的邻居，因为真正的标准是能力。

abstract.en: If music is the art, the musician is the pair of hands that makes the art audible.
abstract.cn: 如果说音乐是那门艺术，音乐家就是让艺术变得可听的那双手。

examples.en: He spent thirty years as a musician in the city orchestra.
examples.cn: 他在市立管弦乐团当了三十年音乐家。

examples.en: The band's musicians tuned up before the doors opened.
examples.cn: 乐队的乐手们在开门前调好了音。

examples.en: My grandmother was a fine musician and played at every family wedding.
examples.cn: 我祖母是一位出色的音乐人，家里每场婚礼她都演奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪吉申」：缪斯女神一附身，人就成了乐手；记住 musician 是音乐家。

root: musician 由 music 加 -ian 构成，-ian 表示「从事某事的人」；这一构词仿照古法语 musicien，而 music 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica 传入。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person whose life is music; the senses split into the trained professional, the player in a group, and anyone whose gift earns the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以音乐为业的人」；义项分成受过训练的职业音乐家、团体里的乐手，以及凭才华配得上这个称呼的任何人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a player at the keyboard, fingers finding the next note by ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：演奏者坐在琴前，手指凭耳朵找到下一个音。

branches.en: a cellist signing a season contract with an orchestra
branches.cn: 大提琴手与乐团签下一季合同

branches.en: a guitarist tuning backstage while the band waits
branches.cn: 吉他手在后台调音，乐队等着他

branches.en: a quartet on tour with four salaries and one shared van
branches.cn: 四重奏巡演，四份薪水合用一辆车

branches.en: a grandmother playing at a wedding for no fee
branches.cn: 祖母在婚礼上分文不取地演奏

branches.en: a street player whose ear is as sharp as any graduate's
branches.cn: 街头乐手的耳朵不输任何科班出身的人

intro.en: The person noun is music plus -ian, the same suffix that builds historian and librarian; -ship then turns the person into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个指人的名词由 music 加 -ian 构成，同一个后缀也造出 historian、librarian；再加 -ship 则把人变成一种修养。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica is the source of the whole family, and Latin musicus could already name a musician as well as describe music.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 是整族词的源头，而拉丁语 musicus 既能形容音乐，也已经可以指乐师。
